title: Canonical symmetric-degree algebra on the affine basis
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal E$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Define the canonical affine-basis graded algebra $A_X(\mathcal E)$, in the graded algebra interface used for relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj], as follows. For every affine open $U$, set $R_U=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $M_U=\mathcal E(U)$ and $A(U)=\operatorname{Sym}_{R_U}(M_U)$. Its degree-$n$ submodule is $(\operatorname{im}\iota_{M_U})^n$, equivalently the image of the degree-$n$ tensor component [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. Its structural $R_U$-algebra map is the canonical symmetric-algebra unit. For $U\subseteq V$, its restriction is the unique ring homomorphism sending scalars by $R_V\to R_U$ and $\iota_{M_V}(m)$ to $\iota_{M_U}(m|_U)$. These rings identify canonically with the affine sections of the symmetric algebra sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra].

The named well-definedness properties of this construction are that restriction preserves each degree and, since $\mathcal E$ is quasi-coherent, each restriction is coefficientwise base change: $R_U\otimes_{R_V} A(V)_n\to A(U)_n$, $r\otimes a\mapsto r\,a|_U$, is an isomorphism for every $n$. Restriction identities and composition are inherited from the symmetric-algebra presheaf. The homogeneous decomposition is the unique inverse of the summation map of the internal direct sum, and the rings, grades and restriction homomorphisms are the specified formulas, not data chosen from an existence assertion.
